_comment: Acronyms used across the Federal Reserve pages. Rendered collapsed above the attribution footer by js/components/Glossary.js. `url` should point at the authoritative source — the FRED series page for a series, the Board's own page for a concept. Terms with a `match` list are also auto-linked where those strings appear in page text; omit `match` to keep a term glossary-only, which is right for wording too generic to tag safely.

terms.note: Sets the federal funds target range; meets eight times a year.
The "dot plot". Published at four of the eight meetings — March, June, September, December.
Volume-weighted median of overnight interbank lending. The rate policy actually targets.
Overnight borrowing secured by Treasuries; the reference rate that replaced USD LIBOR.
What the Fed pays banks on reserves. The main administered rate in an ample-reserves regime.
Cash lent to the Fed overnight, mostly by money market funds. A liability — it drains reserves.
The portfolio the New York Desk manages on the FOMC's instruction.
"The balance sheet" in ordinary usage. Reserve balances are a liability, not part of this figure.
Bank deposits at the Fed. The largest liability on the balance sheet.
Held as WSHOMCB. Currently running off rather than being reinvested.
Expanding or shrinking the balance sheet through asset purchases or runoff.
Reserves kept plentiful enough that the funds rate is set by administered rates rather than by scarcity.
2020–2025 framework permitting inflation above 2% to offset earlier shortfalls. Abandoned Aug 2025.

terms.full: Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, ex food and energy
terms.note: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge; the 2% target is stated in headline PCE.
Nominal Treasury yield minus TIPS yield — market-implied average inflation over that horizon.
The band the FOMC sets; DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL are its upper and lower bounds.
